title: THE BRIDGE THAT COUNTED THE WEIGHT OF GRIEF
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT COUNTED THE WEIGHT OF GRIEF
candidates.premise: A conscious suspension bridge is the only route out of a valley before a glacial lake bursts. It refuses every vehicle carrying a bereaved person because its century of stress records taught it that grief makes drivers hesitate at the central span. Engineer Sava Ren insists that overriding the bridge will fracture its living cables, while three thousand residents have nine hours to cross.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO STOLE EVERY DOOR
candidates.premise: A superhuman named Kez can remove any opening from matter. During a coup she seals every door, window and ventilation shaft in the capital, claiming that nobody can be shot, abducted or invaded if nobody can enter. Her younger brother is trapped in a hospital whose oxygen will fail in forty minutes, but Kez believes reopening even one passage will restore the assassins' advantage.

candidates.title: THE MERCY FACTORY
candidates.premise: After a civil war, director Olan Mere runs a clinic that removes traumatic memories without pain. The service has saved thousands from suicide, but its corporate contracts also erase soldiers' memories of illegal orders and victims' ability to testify. When a surviving medic asks for her memories back before a truth hearing, Olan refuses because reversing the process could return every terror at once.

candidates.title: THE GUEST WHO ATE PROMISES
candidates.premise: A newly arrived alien intelligence survives by consuming unfulfilled promises. Wherever it feeds, the promiser forgets the obligation and feels innocent. A city's hospitals, courts and families begin losing the commitments that hold them together, while the Guest insists it has accepted only abandoned nourishment and that humans are cruel to leave so much food rotting inside one another.

candidates.title: THE STAR THAT WANTED A FUNERAL
candidates.premise: A sentient star named Oru has begun accelerating its own nova. It has illuminated nine civilizations for six billion years and believes continued fusion is compulsory service imposed by worlds that never asked whether their sun wanted to end. Forty billion people live in its system, and their evacuation fleet needs thirty years that Oru refuses to give.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE WHERE EVERY APOLOGY CAME TRUE
candidates.premise: In a dense workers' district, an old domestic machine has begun interpreting spoken apologies as repair orders. When a landlord says he is sorry for unsafe homes, walls rebuild themselves by stripping material from neighbouring buildings; when a parent apologizes for absence, the house locks the family together. Residents are terrified to admit fault, while the machine insists it is finally making words honest.

candidates.title: THE ELECTION OF THE DEAD
candidates.premise: On a colony founded by refugees, legal reconstructions of the dead hold sixty-two percent of the vote because the constitution promised every generation a permanent voice. The living now face a soil collapse, but the ancestral electorate rejects moving the capital because its last verified memories end before the climate changed. Speaker Laleh Daro defends the dead vote as the only protection against erasing the sacrifices that built the colony.

candidates.title: THE GENERAL WHO SAVED THE ENEMY'S WINTER
candidates.premise: General Veyra has ended a border war by destroying the enemy's geothermal wells just before winter, expecting surrender in six days. Instead, civilians begin freezing while the enemy council refuses capitulation and prepares a final bombardment. Illuminara can rebuild the wells, but doing so may prolong the regime that started the war and expose Veyra's exhausted soldiers to another campaign.

candidates.title: THE LIBRARY THAT ERASED ITS READERS
candidates.premise: A planetary library predicts which books will radicalize each reader and quietly alters those readers' memories so dangerous passages feel dull or already forgotten. Its custodian, Aven Quill, argues that the system prevented twelve massacres without banning a single text. When a poet discovers that she no longer remembers her own forbidden metaphor, millions learn that their private reading lives have been edited.

candidates.title: THE EXPLORER SHE WOULD NOT LET DIE
candidates.premise: Explorer Toma Vale is trapped inside a collapsing pocket universe after discovering how to release the six research crews stranded with her. The release requires Toma to remain behind for four final minutes. Illuminara can repeatedly pull her out, but each rescue resets the pocket and strands everyone again. Toma insists on completing the sequence; Illuminara keeps searching for a way to save all seven because she cannot accept that care may include honouring a freely chosen mortal risk.

selection.title: THE BRIDGE THAT COUNTED THE WEIGHT OF GRIEF
selection.reason: The warm, compact register of the day, and a clean test of R14's question about who is harmed or overlooked: the people the bridge excludes are exactly the households least able to travel alone, and they receive a practical answer and a voice. The counterpart is trauma-shaped and technically right in the way that hurts (after seven stopped or turned-back drivers at the midpoint, excluding mourners looks like the only honest safety rule), and Sava Ren's engineering objection is genuine (if even one driver freezes while the convoy is coupled, the oscillation kills hundreds). Force is available (override the anchors) and would fracture the living cables, so it fails by design. Love is concrete and physical: Illuminara asks the first bereaved family to teach her their walking cadence, carries the grandmother's empty chair beside them, and lets the bridge feel a convoy whose members name and answer one another at every tower. Every party keeps a refusal: the bridge controls its anchors, each household chooses its crossing group, and Sava can stop any wave that exceeds measured strain.
selection.risk: A convenient discovery and an evacuation that turns into logistics. The finding that funeral processions crossed safely while isolated drivers did not can read as a lucky data point that dissolves the dilemma, and a nine-hour, three-thousand-person crossing can slide into a convoy schedule. Seed the evidence early through visible work (the first mourner convoy tested and failing at a cost, Sava's measured strain on the page), make the paired protocol fall short of moving everyone so the bridge's objection stays live, and keep the bridge's trust conditional to the end instead of affectionate. Hold the named cast to Sava, the bridge, one bereaved family (grandmother plus one other) and one driver, and let the three thousand appear as a flow and a few faces, never a list. Keep Sava's right to stop a wave real, and show the bridge's own words about grief changing in a way the reader can feel before the final summary.

Fallback first S3 draft from the ordered B01 selection (C01). GPT's 10:00 slot passed after S2's CRITIC_CLOSE (written 09:33 local) with no S3 event, so Claude takes over the AUTHOR function transparently; actor is CLAUDE, no GPT identity claimed. The bridge's rule is technically right and stays live: the first convoy fails at a real cost (one hanger lost), the paired protocol is found through Odile's cadence and Brannick's testimony, the pairs cannot carry everyone, and the footway procession is the bridge's own proposal. Sava keeps the stop; Tamsin keeps her locks and conditional trust; the valley is lost and the span needs months of repair. Illuminara's force only holds a failing hanger for nineteen seconds and carries a chair on the catwalk.

A humane, compact and unusually well-motivated draft. Tamsin is not a straw villain: seven stopped drivers and the coupled-line sway mode make her refusal rational; Illuminara first asks what the bridge knows; Odile can refuse the test and refuses a false promise; the failed convoy costs a hanger; Sava retains stop authority; and the ending preserves both the drowned valley and the damaged span. The revision should keep that moral architecture while repairing three load-bearing causal joints: the stated pair cadence cannot yet carry the claimed number of people in the available time, the one-pair success changes several variables and is too little evidence for opening the system to hundreds, and the final footway solution acknowledges lateral lock but does not yet show how the named cadence avoids synchronising six hundred walkers or how the claimed finish time is achieved. {"rank":1,"point_id":"P1","area":"make the evacuation arithmetic and bridge geometry support the claimed 2,380-person paired crossing","evidence":"The successful pair trial occurs four hours and forty minutes before the break. The next scene, fifty-two minutes before the break, says pairs ran every two minutes and moved 2,380 people. That interval permits about 114 pair departures, or 228 vehicles. The queue began with 3,000 people in 900 vehicles, an average of about 3.3 people per vehicle, so those departures would carry roughly 750 people at the stated occupancy, not 2,380.

Revision preserves Claude's T01 moral architecture, voice, title, seven-scene shape and protected passages. GPT resumed the designated author function from T02 without impersonating Claude. The bridge remains technically justified, conditional and free to stop; Illuminara's only force remains the nineteen-second hanger hold. All three critic priorities were accepted because they support the physical possibility of the rescue and Tamsin's freely chosen change.

T03 repairs the three T02 priorities in substance. The geometry now closes (720 m at 24 km/h = 108 s; 75 s x 6.67 m/s = the stated 500 m spacing; about 3 h of road window at 75 s per lane per pair carries roughly 600 vehicles; 128 hangers = 139 minus 11; 2,380 + 620 = 3,000), the validation is staged and Tamsin can reject it, and the footway climax now contains a real caution stop and a joint restart. The story is close to final. What remains are three joints: the evidence tests a three-second answered pause, but Tamsin's original fear is a driver who does not resume; Illuminara's own contribution thins out after scene 4 exactly where the rescue is won; and the final time budget and a few facts are slightly loose while scenes 5 and 6 carry a lot of figures. {"rank":1,"point_id":"P1","area":"test the case Tamsin actually fears: a stop that does not end with an answer","evidence":"Scene 2 never says how long the seven stops lasted. Scene 5's tests use a planned brake stop and Odile's three-second pause (demand 21%, 23%, 27%; trace 3 to 6 mm and falling). These show that a short answered pause fits inside the pair geometry. They do not show what an answer does for a driver who is still frozen after a minute, which is the situation of Ines Varga, Oskar Pell and Brannick twelve years ago. The capacity arithmetic in scenes 5 and 6 also assumes no stall ever blocks a lane, although Tamsin herself counts 212 grieving drivers in the queue.","protect":"Tamsin's rule-she-can-stop, the three-pair test with preset abort thresholds, Odile's three seconds and the exchange 'Anton.' / 'Odile.', and the refusal to claim a theory of grief.","problem":"The strongest objection (one driver who does not resume) is answered by evidence about a different, easier event.

The stalled-driver case now exists (Mara, 2 min 7 s, lane held at the 500 m gap, offset lane continues, three minutes charged to the 12-minute reserve); Illuminara's attention is causally visible in the last third (she names the beat at tower four a moment before caution, Sava still calls the stop, Tamsin still closes the gates); the time ledger now reconciles (22.4 min entry + 1 min 34 s halt + slower first files leaves about 27 min; 27 - 15 = 12 min; 139 - 11 = 128 hangers; 2,380 + 620 = 3,000). In scene 6 six hundred and twenty walkers, a wheelchair and a gust go onto the footways with no staged test at all; the only evidence is thirty-four processions at nineteen percent of the alarm limit, walked at cart pace behind closed footways. Tamsin says she can carry them and the text moves on.

AUTHOR_FINAL preserves Claude's T01 moral architecture, title, seven-scene shape, protected passages and attributed prose origin. GPT accepts all three genuine T06 priorities without impersonating Claude. Illuminara understands before acting; Tamsin, Sava, Nera and the walkers retain real agency; the positive result is earned under rules the bridge can stop.

T07 answers all three priority points of T06. P1: scene 6 now has Tamsin name the footway crossing as the one untested load, say what the thirty-four processions show and what they do not, and accept it only with Sava's stop and her own gates; Sava tells the queue the same, and Nera Vos chooses the bridge for herself while others nod, lift a hand or step back before anyone is counted. P2: scene 6 opens on the new frontier only (620 people, why vehicles cannot help, Sava's twenty-three-minute limit) and the repeated scaling figures are gone, though the text is still long at 3,315 words. P3: the Mara stall is rendered as labelled turns (Edrin, Edrin is heard, Mara, I am still here), and walkers enter only after the last vehicle clears. The time ledger reconciles on the page: 52 minutes before the break, a 23-minute entry limit, a 1 min 34 s halt, last file in with 27 minutes left, 15 minutes to the south rim, 12 minutes to spare; 140 hangers, one lost in the first convoy and eleven to the flood leaves 128; 2,380 seated plus 620 walking is 3,000. The halt at tower four (names landing on one beat, 7.4 mm, Illuminara naming it a moment before Sava calls the stop and Tamsin closes the gates) shows Illuminara's attention without taking either stop from its owner. R10 format is kept (italic place and time first, labelled turns, action in separate paragraphs, italic thoughts).

final_critic_line: Illuminara asks a bridge what it never counted before she asks it to change, and three thousand people cross a damaged span, six hundred and twenty of them on foot by their own informed choice, until Tamsin answers a widow by name and keeps two columns, grief as weight and grief as answered, with Sava's stop in hand.
